designs.description: 🏺️ The digital shadow of the former Nakagin Capsule Tower which was a mixed-use residential and office tower designed by architect Kisho Kurokawa and located in Shimbashi, Tokyo, Japan. Completed in 1972, the building was a rare remaining example of Japanese Metabolism, an architectural movement emblematic of Japan's postwar cultural resurgence.

items.name: Base Blob
items.description: 🏩️ A blobby two storey office building with an entrance hall and access to the staircases and elevators of the round cores on the groundfloor. It has a setback and a colonade towards the street. On the second floor are the office rooms.

items.name: Single Storey Tambour
items.description:
🪤️ An efficient one storey tambour for a rectangular shaft core with an elevator in the center, the main platform on the north, and on the other corners sides platforms with two doors. There is a stair between 
every platform. The doors are spiraling around.

items.name: Slanted
items.description: 🚕️ A sloped variant of the Nakagin Capsule Tower where the capsules have balconies and the towers are graduated in opposing directions. Each tower has a direction and every floor is stepped in this direction.

items.name: Twisted
items.description: 🚙️ A twisted variant of the Nakagin Capsule Tower where the capsules are trapezoids and towers are round with the floors twisting in one direction.

items.name: Dancing
items.description: 🚓️ The expolsion axonometry of a futuristic variant of the Nakagin Capsule Tower where two towers are dancing with each other. The capsules are ellipsoids around a round shaft and a blob base.

items.name: Flat
items.description: 🚑️ The digital shadow of the former Nakagin Capsule Tower which was a mixed-use residential and office tower designed by architect Kisho Kurokawa and located in Shimbashi, Tokyo, Japan. Completed in 1972, the building was a rare remaining example of Japanese Metabolism, an architectural movement emblematic of Japan's postwar cultural resurgence.
